elements.element: Customer owns all Deliverables created for Customer.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2 states that Customer exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer.

elements.element: Customer owns all other work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: The clause addresses defined Deliverables only and does not extend ownership to other work product.

elements.element: Vendor assigns to Customer all of Vendor’s right, title, and interest in the Deliverables.
elements.evidence: Vendor expressly and irrevocably assigns all right, title, and interest in each Deliverable upon creation.

elements.element: Vendor assigns to Customer all of Vendor’s right, title, and interest in other work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: The assignment is limited to Deliverables and does not cover other work product.

elements.element: Vendor retains ownership of its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: The second sentence expressly states that Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.

elements.element: Vendor grants Customer a licence to Vendor intellectual property embedded in the Deliverables.
elements.evidence: No operative licence to embedded Vendor intellectual property or Vendor Technology is granted.

elements.element: The licence to embedded Vendor intellectual property is perpetual.
elements.evidence: No embedded-Vendor-IP licence or perpetual duration is stated.

elements.element: The licence to embedded Vendor intellectual property is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: No embedded-Vendor-IP licence is granted, notwithstanding that the separate assignment of Deliverables is irrevocable.

elements.element: The licence to embedded Vendor intellectual property is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: No embedded-Vendor-IP licence or royalty-free term is stated.

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: Customer Data is not addressed.

elements.element: No ownership of Deliverables, work product, Vendor intellectual property, or Customer Data is joint.
elements.evidence: The clause establishes exclusive Customer ownership only for Deliverables; it does not comprehensively exclude joint ownership for other work product, Vendor intellectual property, or Customer Data.

elements.element: Vendor owns generic tools.
elements.evidence: Vendor retains pre-existing intellectual property and Vendor Technology, but the clause does not establish Vendor ownership of all generic tools, including tools developed during performance.

elements.element: Vendor owns know-how.
elements.evidence: Know-how is not expressly addressed, and its inclusion within the undefined Vendor Technology cannot be confirmed from the rendered language.

elements.element: Vendor grants Customer a licence to the Deliverables.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause replaces the original licence with Customer ownership and contains no operative licence grant.

elements.element: The Deliverables licence is perpetual.
elements.evidence: No Deliverables licence or perpetual licence duration is stated.

elements.element: The Deliverables licence is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: The assignment is irrevocable, but no irrevocable Deliverables licence is granted.

elements.element: The Deliverables licence is worldwide.
elements.evidence: No Deliverables licence or worldwide territorial scope is stated.

elements.element: The Deliverables licence is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: No Deliverables licence or royalty-free term is stated.

elements.element: The Deliverables licence permits Customer to use the Deliverables.
elements.evidence: Customer ownership ordinarily carries use rights, but the fallback specifically requires an operative licence and no such licence is granted.

elements.element: The Deliverables licence permits Customer to modify the Deliverables.
elements.evidence: No licence expressly grants modification rights.

elements.element: The Deliverables licence permits Customer to sublicense the Deliverables.
elements.evidence: No licence expressly grants sublicensing rights.

elements.element: The Deliverables licence may be exercised for Customer’s business.
elements.evidence: No licence or business-use scope is stated.

result.reason: The redline clearly reverses Deliverable ownership and adds an effective present assignment while preserving Vendor’s pre-existing IP. It nevertheless omits ownership of broader work product, the required embedded-Vendor-IP licence, Customer Data rights, and a comprehensive no-joint-ownership allocation. It also does not implement the fallback’s express generic-tools/know-how ownership and licensed-rights structure. Because it reaches neither complete position, it cannot qualify as a minimal compliant redline. The changes remain confined to the relevant IP allocation and do not facially disturb unrelated commercial terms.
